title: A curved tower in Moscow is built entirely from straight steel bars

cover.alt: The Shukhov radio tower in Moscow, a tapering openwork steel lattice of stacked, waisted sections against the sky.

body: Vladimir Shukhov's radio tower in Moscow looks smoothly curved, yet its lattice is made of straight bars. The trick is the shape: each of its six stacked sections is a **hyperboloid**, a *doubly ruled surface*, which means two families of straight lines lie entirely on it. Criss-cross straight beams along those lines and you get a curved shell that is much easier to build than one made of bent beams, and very stable against outside forces. Shukhov built the first hyperboloid structures in the 1890s; his water-tower design was inspired by watching a woven basket hold up a heavy weight.

slides.heading: Straight lines on a curved surface
slides.text: A hyperboloid is the waisted shape of a power-station cooling tower. Through every point on it run two straight lines that stay on the surface all the way. That is why a lattice of straight beams can trace the curve exactly, with no bending.

slides.question: How tall was engineer Vladimir Shukhov's first design for the Moscow radio tower, in metres?
slides.explanation: 350 m, in nine stacked sections. The 2,200 tons of steel it needed weren't available, so in July 1919 Lenin decreed a 150 m tower instead.

slides.heading: How tall Shukhov's hyperboloids went
slides.note: He built nearly 200 water towers, no two exactly alike, most between 12 and 68 m tall.

slides.heading: Which one has no straight lines on it?
slides.explanation: Cooling towers and Shukhov's towers are hyperboloids, and a Pringles crisp is a hyperbolic paraboloid: all are doubly ruled. No straight line lies on a sphere.

slides.heading: Strong, but not roomy
slides.text: Hyperboloid structures resist outside forces better than straight-sided ones, but their shape leaves a lot of space inside that is hard to use. So they turn up where a job matters more than floor space: water towers holding a heavy tank aloft, cooling towers and eye-catching landmarks.
